chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from his father, raising it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The beautiful woman cuts the phlegm, and the ugly woman stirs the black bile.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْبَلْغَم: Phlegm, one of the four major humors in classical medicine, associated with cold and moist qualities.
key_terms.الْمِرَّة: Bile, specifically referring to black bile in this context, associated with dryness and coldness.
key_terms.الْمِرَّةَ السَّوْدَاءَ: Black bile, a humor believed to cause melancholy or specific temperamental dispositions.

ai.seo_question: What is the physiological effect of beauty and ugliness on the body's humors according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reflects the classical Greco-Arabic theory of humors (al-Tabi'at al-Arba'), linking physical aesthetics to internal physiological balance. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted not merely as superficial judgment but as an indicator of inner temperament, where beauty signifies a harmonious flow of bodily fluids and 'ugliness' suggests an accumulation of melancholic black bile. This perspective underscores the holistic view of the human body in Islamic medicine, where external appearance is seen as a mirror of internal health and character.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Abu Al Qasim, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The beautiful woman cuts the phlegm and the terrible woman stirs the black bile’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn abu al-Qasim from his father in a marfu’ manner who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A good looking woman cuts down phlegm and an ugly looking woman excites black bile.’”
